Live hardware checks (recap)

Performed against this Mac's real disk and the real hosted Gateway, not the sandbox:

  • Upgrade-in-place: the machine's genuine v1.7.1 “CC Director.app” was replaced by one canonical Director.app. Seeded Finder duplicates in both Applications folders were purged; a seeded foreign app named “Director 2.app” with another vendor's bundle id survived untouched.
  • Launch: on the unlocked console, Director.app launched exactly the way the wizard's button launches it — main window rendered, Dock application connection registered under com.devthrottle.ccdirector, hosted Gateway tunnel dialed — then shut down cleanly through its Control API.
[MainWindow] Avalonia MainWindow initialized
[ControlApiHost] Kestrel listening on http://127.0.0.1:7879
[GatewayStreamClient] Start: dialing https://devthrottle-gw.azurewebsites.net
POST /shutdown → {"accepted":true} — process exited, no crash journal

The DMG and the new icon

v1.7.3 adds devthrottle-mac-arm64.dmg: open, drag Director onto the Applications shortcut, done — manual installs land in one canonical place instead of scattering copies. The zip remains the auto-updater's asset. The app icon is now a “D” (the app is named Director), keeping the dark squircle and blue prompt accent:

The one cosmetic item: the menu bar

When the Director is the frontmost app, the bold app menu next to the Apple logo — where Finder says “Finder” and Safari says “Safari” — reads “Avalonia Application” instead of “Director”. That name comes from the app framework's runtime default when the app builds its native menu, not from the bundle (whose name is correctly “Director” everywhere else: Dock, Spotlight, Launchpad, Finder). It has been this way in every prior version too — not a regression, just newly noticed during launch verification:

lsappinfo: "CFBundleIdentifier"="com.devthrottle.ccdirector"
           "LSDisplayName"="Avalonia Application"   ← the menu-bar name

Small follow-up fix in the app's menu-building code; cosmetic only. Say the word and an issue gets filed.

Environment notes

  • The launcher row's red “Failed” in this run is a development-machine artifact (port 7900 already owned by your real launcher). The engine, download, and placement all succeeded.
  • The DMG packaging runs in CI for the first time on the v1.7.3 tag — worth watching that job once.
